summary: The GAIA variant is a feature-rich multi-agent system built on the SPADE framework. While it provides a clear and comprehensive agent architecture with 9 specialized agents, it is currently in a prototype state with simulated LLM logic and significant security flaws.

findings.description: Hardcoded OpenAI API key in the main system class constructor.
Weak hardcoded passwords used for all agents in the multi-agent system.
LLM integration is simulated using basic keyword matching instead of actual model inference.
findings.evidence: def extract_symptoms(self, text): ... keywords = ["fever", "cough", ...] in LLMProcessorAgent

findings.description: Health data persistence is limited to in-memory lists, preventing long-term data analysis and scalability.
Well-structured multi-agent communication using SPADE's message subjects.
findings.evidence: if msg.subject == "AggregateHealthData": await self.analyze_patterns(...) in HealthAnalyzerAgent

missing_requirements: Skalowalność: System uses in-memory storage and localhost XMPP, which is not suitable for high concurrent loads without external DB and broker config.
Bezpieczeństwo: No encryption or data protection for user health data beyond simple agent passwords.
implementation_risks: Hardcoded API keys lead to immediate credential exposure.
Lack of persistent storage means all health data is lost on system restart.
Keyword-based symptom extraction will fail on complex natural language inputs.
